title: We were not among those who prayed.
subtitle: The first answer is about prayer
then: Asked what brought them into Saqar, the very first thing they name is prayer. Ibn Kathir summarises it as {trap}we did not worship Allah{/trap}. Before any other failure, this one comes first.
now: Asr slips by during a meeting. Maghrib is lost in traffic. Isha waits until you are too tired. {idea}Of everything they could have said first, they said prayer.{/idea} It is the daily thread that holds the rest together.
old: Missing a prayer here and there is not a big deal.
new: Prayer is the first thing named on that Day, so I guard it first now.
try: Set an alarm for the next prayer today and pray it as soon as it goes off.

title: And we did not feed the poor.
subtitle: Faith that never reached a hungry person
then: Ibn Kathir explains the two answers together: {trap}we did not worship Allah, nor did we do good to His creatures{/trap}. Prayer and feeding the poor stand side by side, one toward Allah, one toward people.
now: You pass the same man outside the station every morning. The food bank box at the supermarket is half empty. {idea}Feeding someone is named right after prayer.{/idea} A sandwich can be part of your faith.
old: My faith is between me and Allah; other people's hunger is not my concern.
new: Feeding the hungry stands right beside prayer in how I will be asked.
try: Buy or share one meal today with someone who needs it.

title: We waded into empty talk with the talkers.
subtitle: Going astray because everyone else did
then: Ibn Kathir says it means {trap}we used to speak about what we had no knowledge of{/trap}. Qatadah said: {trap}every time someone went astray, we went astray with them{/trap}.
now: The group chat is tearing into someone. A thread is mocking religion. You did not start it, but you add a laugh, a hot take, a share. {idea}Wading in is a choice, even when the water was already there.{/idea}
old: I only joined a conversation that was already happening.
new: Going along with empty or false talk is my own deed, not just theirs.
try: Next time a conversation turns to gossip or mockery today, change the subject or leave.

title: And we called the Day of Recompense a lie.
subtitle: The root under every other failure
then: Their list ends with the root: {trap}we used to deny the Day of Recompense{/trap}. If there is no reckoning, prayer, feeding the poor and careful speech all feel optional.
now: When you truly believe the bill is coming, you budget. When you do not, you spend. {idea}Belief in the Day is what makes the small good habits make sense.{/idea}
old: I believe in the Day of Judgement, even if I rarely think about it.
new: Belief in the Day shows up in how I pray, give and speak this week.
try: Spend two minutes tonight imagining your own reckoning, then do one good deed.

title: Until the certainty came to us.
subtitle: Death ends the time for choosing
then: Ibn Kathir says the certainty here is {idea}death{/idea}, as in the verse: worship your Lord until the certainty comes to you. The same word appears in both: one person worships until death, another denies until death.
now: The phone call from the hospital at an ordinary hour. A colleague who was there last Friday and not this one. {idea}The certainty does not book an appointment.{/idea} Until it comes, you can still change your answer.
old: I will sort out my faith properly once I am older.
new: Death is the one certainty, so the time to choose is before it.
try: Make one sincere tawbah today, as if this were your last ordinary day.

title: No intercessor's plea will help them.
subtitle: Intercession has conditions
then: Ibn Kathir explains that {idea}intercession is only useful if its conditions are met{/idea}. For those with these traits, who come before Allah as disbelievers, the plea of any intercessor {trap}will be of no benefit{/trap}.
now: You picture someone vouching for you: a righteous parent, a scholar you love. {idea}Hope in intercession is real, but it is not a replacement for showing up.{/idea} Bring belief and prayer with you.
old: Someone good will speak up for me, whatever I do.
new: Intercession helps those who came as believers, so I build on belief myself.
try: Send blessings on the Prophet ﷺ ten times today and ask Allah to accept you.

title: So what is wrong with them, turning from the reminder?
subtitle: The puzzle of refusing good advice

picture.label: What is in front of them

then: After hearing the conversation from that Day, the Quran turns back to the listeners in Makkah. Ibn Kathir paraphrases: {trap}what is wrong with these people who turn away{/trap} from what you are calling them to? They had just been told the answers.
now: The reminder notification pops up: time to read. You swipe it away. Again. {idea}The question is asked to you too: what is wrong, that you keep turning?{/idea} Asked gently, it can open something.
old: I am not turning away from Allah, I am just busy.
new: Swiping away reminders again and again is a kind of turning away I can notice.
try: The next reminder you get today, a notification or a friend's word, act on it immediately.

title: Like startled wild donkeys.
subtitle: Panic in the wrong direction
then: Ibn Kathir describes them {trap}fleeing from the truth and turning away from it{/trap}, like wild donkeys bolting. The Arabs knew this sight well: a herd scattering in blind panic across open land.
now: A friend starts to talk about salah and you suddenly have to go. A khutbah gets serious and you check your phone. {trap}The bolt is quick and almost automatic.{/trap} Notice it, and sit still a moment longer.
old: Avoiding uncomfortable reminders keeps me calm.
new: Bolting from the truth is panic in the wrong direction.
try: The next time a reminder makes you want to leave, stay for one more minute and listen.

title: Fleeing from a lion.
subtitle: They treat their cure as a predator
then: Abu Hurayrah and Ibn Abbas said Qaswarah is {trap}the lion{/trap}. Ibn Abbas noted it has a name in many languages. The image: people running from the reminder as if it were a lion hunting them, when it was {reward}the thing trying to save them{/reward}.
now: Avoiding the doctor because you fear what they will say. Not opening the bank statement. {idea}Running from the thing that could help is a very human habit.{/idea} The Quran is not the lion.
old: Facing the truth about myself feels like being hunted.
new: The reminder is not a predator; it is the hand reaching out to help.
try: Open one thing you have been avoiding today: a verse, a bill, a message.

title: Each wants his own scripture, delivered to him personally.
subtitle: Demanding special proof before believing
then: Mujahid and others said each wanted {trap}a book revealed to him{/trap} as it was to the Prophet ﷺ. Qatadah said they wanted to be declared innocent {trap}without having to do any deeds{/trap}. Allah knows best where to place His message.
now: If Allah gave me a clear sign, I would change. If I had a dream, if a miracle happened. {trap}Waiting for a personal delivery{/trap} while the message is already in your hands.
old: If I got a personal sign, I would finally take faith seriously.
new: The message has already come to me; waiting for my own is a way to delay.
try: Stop waiting for a sign today: read one page of the Quran as if it were addressed to you.

title: No. The truth is, they do not fear the Hereafter.
subtitle: The real reason behind the excuses
then: Ibn Kathir explains that {trap}they were only corrupted by their lack of faith in it{/trap} and their rejection that it would happen. The demand for a personal scripture was a cover. The real issue was they did not fear the Hereafter.
now: I will start praying properly once I understand it better. Once work calms down. Once I am married. {idea}Sometimes the reasons are real. Sometimes they are covering a quieter truth: I am not worried enough about the Hereafter.{/idea}
old: My reasons for delaying are practical, nothing more.
new: Under my excuses, I can ask honestly how much I fear the Hereafter.
try: Write down your main excuse for one delayed good deed, and ask if it is the real reason.

title: No. This Quran is a reminder.
subtitle: Not magic, not a man's words

picture.label: What they called it, what it is

then: Al-Walid had called the Quran magic and the words of a man. The surah closes with Allah's own answer: {idea}truly the Quran is a reminder{/idea}. Ibn Kathir notes it simply. A reminder brings back what the heart already knows.
now: A sticky note on the fridge. A calendar alert for your mother's birthday. {idea}A reminder does not teach you something new. It brings back what matters before you forget.{/idea} That is what the Quran does each time you open it.
old: The Quran is a book I need to study before it can affect me.
new: The Quran is a reminder, and even a little of it brings my heart back.
try: Put one short verse somewhere you will see it every day this week.

title: So whoever wills will remember it.
subtitle: The reminder waits for you to want it
then: Ibn Kathir reads it plainly: {idea}whosoever wills receives admonition from it{/idea}. The same open door as verse 37, to go forward or stay behind. The reminder is offered to everyone.
now: The Quran sits on the shelf or in the app. It does not jump into your hands. {idea}It waits for you to want it.{/idea} Wanting it, even a little, is where remembering begins.
old: If I were meant to be reminded, it would just happen to me.
new: The reminder is there; my wanting it is the part I bring.
try: Tell Allah honestly today: I want to remember You. Help me.

title: He is worthy of fear, and the One who forgives.
subtitle: The surah ends on forgiveness
then: No one remembers unless Allah wills, like the verse: you cannot will unless Allah wills. Then the last words. Qatadah said He {idea}deserves to be feared{/idea} and He is {reward}the One who forgives whoever turns to Him and repents{/reward}. A surah full of warning ends here.
now: You have read about the Trumpet, Saqar, the people of the right, the excuses. Maybe you saw yourself in a few lines. {reward}The very last word is forgiveness.{/reward} Fear is meant to bring you to the door, not to stop you at it.
old: After all these warnings, I am too far gone to be forgiven.
new: He is worthy of fear and ready to forgive, so I turn to Him now.
try: Say Astaghfirullah slowly a hundred times today, spread across the day.
